title: Requests of assisted suicide from older people in inpatient and outpatient long-term care - professional care handling and suicide prevention
summary: In the national debate on assisted suicide and suicide prevention, the specific role and responsibility of the nursing profession has hardly been addressed to date. In contrast, nursing professionals are often consulted as the first point of contact when people in need of care express a wish for assisted suicide. Particularly in the inpatient and outpatient long-term care of older people, the responsibility of care professionals in dealing professionally with requests for suicide assistance and in suicide prevention is evident. The project addresses the national research gap on dealing with requests for suicide assistance and the role of nursing professionals in suicide prevention. As part of the research project, two instruments are being developed to support professional, ethically based action: Practice Guidelines and Ethics Guidelines. The aim is to ensure that the professional actions of nursing staff in confronting and dealing with requests for suicide assistance and in suicide prevention work are professionally sound and ethically reflective. As a result, the project supports the quality of care in both inpatient and outpatient long-term care facilities and services and, at best, protects human lives through the intended strengthening of suicide prevention.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
a.) Nursing staff (three-year trained or academically qualified nursing staff with state recognition as a nursing specialist, as a health and pediatric nurse, as a geriatric nurse, as a pediatric nurse)
b.) At the time of the focus group and the Delphi survey, active work in long-term care, in the care and treatment of residents (inpatient) or patients (outpatient)
c.) German language skills that are sufficient to ensure that the nursing staff, as potential participants, can fully understand the content of the educational and information letter in order to ensure voluntary and informed participation, as well as active participation in the focus group, and that the questionnaire content can be recorded as part of the Delphi survey waves (online) and the survey of self-efficacy expectations (online)
d.) Ability to give informed consent throughout the entire survey period - written consent to participate in the focus group as well as consent in the context of the online surveys and survey using online questionnaires).
Exclusion criteria:
All persons who do not fall under the above inclusion criteria.
